title.en: Rolling without slipping and the inertia race

summary: Race bodies of equal mass and radius down one incline so the only difference is where their mass sits.
objective: Build an incline race where a hoop, a solid cylinder and a sphere roll without slipping and their accelerations differ by moment of inertia alone.
intent_signals: Show why a hoop loses a rolling race to a sphere.
Explain rolling without slipping with a visible contact condition.
example_prompts: Build a rolling race down an incline with hoop, cylinder and sphere and a live speed comparison.
Show what happens when the incline is too steep for rolling without slipping.
negative_signals: Not a deformable contact or rolling-resistance model.
Not a claim about real objects with bearings, air drag or surface texture.
not_for: Not a deformable contact or rolling-resistance model.
Not a claim about real objects with bearings, air drag or surface texture.

entities.name: Rolling bodies
entities.guidance: Give each body a visible surface marker so rotation is countable and slipping would be obvious.

entities.name: Incline and contact
entities.guidance: Model the incline with a stated angle and draw the contact point with the friction requirement displayed.

entities.name: Comparison readout
entities.guidance: Show the mass distribution factor, the resulting acceleration and the current speed for each body side by side.

state_contract.model: Rigid bodies with positive mass m, radius R and inertia factor k = I/(m R squared), rolling without slipping on a rigid incline at angle theta in the interval from 0 up to but excluding a right angle, so the centre-of-mass acceleration is g sin(theta)/(1 + k) and rolling requires a static friction coefficient of at least k tan(theta)/(1 + k). Angular velocity follows from the rolling condition. When the friction requirement is exceeded the race enters a declared rolling-model-invalid state and freezes rather than inventing an unmodelled sliding branch.
state_contract.authority: The rolling condition ties rotation to translation: the visual spin is computed from travelled distance, never animated independently.
actions: Start, pause and reset the race.
Change the incline angle and watch the friction requirement.
Reduce the friction coefficient until the requirement fails and the rolling-model-invalid state is reported.
Toggle the surface markers and readouts.

invariants: Centre-of-mass speed equals radius times angular speed for every body while rolling.

Bodies with a larger inertia factor k accelerate less, independent of mass and radius, and the finish order follows k only for a simultaneous release from rest on a common incline with the angle held fixed for the whole run.

When the friction requirement is exceeded the scene enters the rolling-model-invalid state, freezes the affected body and says so; it does not continue with an independent spin and translation that no equation in this recipe defines.
motion_guidance: Derive spin from travelled distance so the surface marker never drifts relative to the ground.
Keep all bodies released at the same instant from the same line so the comparison is fair and visible.
known_limits: Idealised rigid contact: no deformation, rolling resistance or air drag.
The slipping transition is reported as a state change, not simulated as a full friction contact model.
Changing the incline angle mid-run invalidates the constant-acceleration comparison, so the scene pauses and resets the race when the angle is edited.
Authored guidance only: no scene runtime, rendering or numerical calibration has been run for this recipe.

claims.statement: For rolling without slipping the velocity of the centre of mass equals the radius times the angular velocity about the axis.
claims.scope: Rigid body on a rigid surface as cited.

claims.statement: The centre-of-mass acceleration of a body rolling down an incline is reduced by its rotational inertia term, so bodies with mass further from the axis accelerate less, and rolling without slipping requires a static friction coefficient at least as large as a stated expression involving the incline angle and that inertia term.
claims.scope: Rigid symmetric bodies on a rigid incline as cited; deformation and rolling resistance are excluded.

source_refs.locator: 11.1, acceleration on an incline and static friction condition

object_craft.structure: Distinct geometry per body with a painted radial stripe and a rim marker so rotation and slip are visible.
object_craft.material: Same base material across bodies so only geometry differs; the stripe is a high-contrast decal, not a light effect.
object_craft.articulation: Rotation angle is computed from travelled distance while rolling; in the rolling-model-invalid state the body freezes and is flagged, rather than being animated with an undefined independent spin.

object_craft.structure: A ramp with a measured angle indicator and a contact patch marker under each body.
object_craft.material: Matte ramp with a subtle grid so travelled distance is readable.
object_craft.articulation: The contact marker follows the body and is highlighted when the friction requirement is exceeded.

physical_contract.scope: Point-contact rigid rolling with an analytic acceleration; no deformation, drag or rolling resistance.
driving: Gravity component along the incline with the rotational inertia term.
contact: Single contact point per body; static friction requirement evaluated each step.
physical_contract.timestep: Fixed simulation step with interpolated rendering.
checks: Speed equals radius times angular speed while the slipping flag is clear.

For simultaneous rest release on one fixed nonzero incline, with all bodies remaining in the valid no-slip branch until completion, finish order follows inertia factor. A frozen invalid-model body has no predicted finish time under this recipe.
